steps.h: Kevin did not answer. Five times.
steps.text: You called Kevin five times. No answer. On call six, he booked a tour. This happens a lot.
Most appointments come after several tries.
steps.sub: So do not stop after one call.

steps.q: A buyer says: "Not for six months." What is that?
steps.why: They told you when. Set a task for it.

steps.text: Nurture means friendly follow-up over time. The sooner they plan to move, the more often you call.

items.text: Two new 3-bed homes came up. Want them?
Are you ready to buy yet?

steps.before: Last time you said your lease ends in March. Is that still the

steps.says: My landlord is selling. I must move in January.

options.text: That is soon! Would Saturday at 10 or Sunday at 2 work?
options.why: A closer date means ask for the appointment.

options.text: OK. I will call you in March.
options.why: His date changed. He is ready now.

steps.q: A lead texts: "STOP CALLING ME." What now?
options: Text one more time to say sorry
steps.why: STOP means stop now. Never argue. Never delete.

steps.text: Every ISA makes mistakes. You book the wrong time. You forget a callback. What matters is the next hour.
Tell your agent fast. Bring the fix.
steps.sub: A hidden mistake breaks trust. A told one builds it.

steps.h: Put your mistake message in order
items: Say what you changed for next time
Say what you need from them

items.text: I missed your call. I am sorry.
The system did not save it.

steps.q: Where do you tell your agent about a mistake?
steps.why: Always the client channel. Your coordinator sees it too.

steps.says: Megan booked a tour. Why did she get a "still looking?" text?

options.text: Sorry, the system does that sometimes.
options.why: That is an excuse. Say it was your mistake.

options.text: My mistake. I forgot the stage. It is fixed, and I texted Megan.
options.why: You say it was you. You bring the fix.

steps.q: You texted a lead at 7 AM their time. What do you do?
steps.why: Rule mistakes go to your coordinator first. Never hide them.

steps.text: Three numbers show your day. Dials, talks and appointments. They are goals. Nobody expects them on day one.

steps.q: You had many talks but no appointments. What do you fix?
options: Ask for a day and time on every call
steps.why: No ask, no appointment. Always offer two times.

steps.text: Your team listens to some of your calls. Each call gets a score out of 100. The goal is 90 or more.

steps.h: Where do the 100 points come from?

cards.back: Did you ask A, L and M?
Did you stay calm and ask again?
Good Follow Up Boss notes. Calling rules followed.

steps.q: Which part has the most points?
steps.why: A.L.M. is 30 points. Always ask for the appointment.

steps.line: I call fast. I ask A, L and M. I write it down. I follow up.

steps.text: Boot camp done! You are ready for your first real calls.

quiz.q: What does a great ISA do?
options: Calls fast, asks A.L.M., writes it down, follows up
quiz.explain: Fast, A.L.M., notes, follow-up. That is the job.

quiz.q: You make a mistake. What do you do first?
options: Wait for the agent to find it
Tell your agent fast, with the fix

quiz.q: How many appointments is a good shift?
quiz.explain: The goal is 2 to 3 per shift.

quiz.q: What score is the goal on the score card?
A lead does not answer your first call. What is true?
options: Keep trying. Most appointments come after several tries.
quiz.explain: Do not stop after one call.
